handback.title: Hotfix PRs labeled, design asks replanned, cards one line
handback.summary: A hotfix's pull request carries its label, a design choice returns it to planning, and its card is one line.
handback.user_story: Owners spot hotfixes by label, see design asks go back to planning, and read each hotfix's card in one line.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker opens its pull request, the pull request carries the hotfix label.
acceptance_criteria.words: Every hotfix PR carries the `hotfix` label

edge_cases.case: An issue without the hotfix label opens its pull request with no hotfix label.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker raises that the ask needs a design choice, the planner starts on the issue.
acceptance_criteria.words: or the worker finds the ask needs a design choice, it goes back to normal planning

edge_cases.case: A hotfix worker that raises nothing still goes to code review.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker sends the issue back to planning, the issue gets a comment saying why.
acceptance_criteria.words: it goes back to normal planning, saying why

edge_cases.case: A hotfix worker that raises nothing posts no such comment.

acceptance_criteria.text: When an issue labeled hotfix is drawn, its card is one line showing its state.

edge_cases.case: A hotfix that blocks another issue still has a one line card.
The card on the pull request is one line too.

acceptance_criteria.text: When an issue labeled hotfix is drawn, its card line shows the ask word for word.
acceptance_criteria.words: The card shows one line: the ask, the PR, the review verdict, the gate.

edge_cases.case: Redrawn after the ask was folded below the card, the line still shows it.
An ask written on two lines shows whole in the one line.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix has a pull request, its card line links that pull request.
acceptance_criteria.words: The card shows one line: the ask, the PR, the review verdict, the gate.

edge_cases.case: With no pull request yet, the line links none.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix code review ends, its card line says code review approved or blocked.
acceptance_criteria.words: The card shows one line: the ask, the PR, the review verdict, the gate.

edge_cases.case: A blocking review shows code review blocked.
Before any review, the line names no verdict.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix merge gate runs, its card line says merge gate passed or failed.
acceptance_criteria.words: The card shows one line: the ask, the PR, the review verdict, the gate.

edge_cases.case: A failed gate shows merge gate failed.
Before the gate runs, the line names no result.

non_functional.text: The hotfix parts of the worker and reviewer prompts name nothing about this project's own repo.
non_functional.why: Prompts must fit any repo Dokima runs on.
non_functional.words: keep the prompts free of anything about Dokima's own repo, so they fit any repo.
non_functional.no_edge_cases: It is one rule on fixed prompt text, checked whole on each run.

test_changes.tests/test_hotfix.py::test_hotfix_prompt: Also proves 864.9; its checks are unchanged, so 863.10 keeps its proof.

raises.label: Doubt: already done
raises.text: Hotfix pull requests already link their issue; a test passing today is refused. Drop that ask? The plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: `agent.yml` opens every worker's pull request with `Closes #N`; the card links the issue; #718 refuses passing tests.
